title: No Signer is wired in the composition root; TenantKeyStore holds only the default algorithm
description:
asterius_domain::Signer has exactly one implementor, asterius_jose::LocalKeyStore, which is used only by tests. main.rs builds a TenantKeyStore and registers it as Arc<dyn KeyStore>; nothing in the binary can sign anything. The first grant handler (ast-a05.2) needs a Signer, so this blocks it.

Two things have to be decided together:

1. What implements Signer over PostgreSQL. crates/store-pg/src/keys.rs deliberately does not: 'Signing through it would mean unwrapping the private key on every token — for a cloud KMS, a network round trip per token. The composition root loads the active key once and signs from memory.' So something has to hold the unwrapped keys.

2. How many keys it holds. After ast-a05.12 a Signer must answer for any SigningAlgorithm a client registered, not just the tenant default — so 'the active key' is now 'the active key per algorithm'. TenantKeyStore::apply_schedule calls apply_schedule(SigningAlgorithm::DEFAULT) and active_signing_key(SigningAlgorithm::DEFAULT); both need to iterate SigningAlgorithm::ALL, or the deployment has to decide which algorithms it offers and refuse registrations for the others (ast-a05.13).

Also unresolved: a cached in-memory signer has to notice a rotation. A key promoted from pending to active by the background sweep must reach the signer, or it keeps signing with a retiring key until the process restarts.
acceptance_criteria: The binary holds an Arc<dyn Signer> that answers for every algorithm the tenant has an active key for, refreshes across a rotation, and returns DomainError::NoSigningKey for an algorithm it has no key for. A test issues a token through it for each algorithm in SigningAlgorithm::ALL.
close_reason: CachedSigner in crates/server/src/signing.rs implements Signer over PgKeyRepository, holding unwrapped keys in memory with a 60s TTL so a rotation on another replica reaches this process without a restart. Wired into the composition root as ClientEndpoints::signer. TenantKeyStore::apply_schedule now provisions and opens an active key for every SigningAlgorithm::ALL, and key_rotation_schedules is keyed per algorithm so rotating one does not suppress the others. Six integration tests in crates/server/tests/signing.rs cover every advertised algorithm, refusal rather than substitution, an empty tenant, cache expiry across a rotation, and a cached miss. Follow-up: ast-mxc.9 (nothing promotes a pending key without a restart).

title: Signer cannot be told which algorithm to sign with (wrong at_hash for ES256/PS256 clients)
description:
Signer::sign takes (tenant, typ, claims) and picks the tenant's active key, preferring EdDSA. An ID token must be signed with the *client's* registered id_token_signed_response_alg: OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 has the client check the algorithm, and §3.1.3.6 ties at_hash to it — the hash is derived from the signing algorithm, so signing with EdDSA while the client expects ES256 produces an at_hash the client computes differently and therefore rejects.

Concretely: a client that registers ES256 or PS256 today gets an ID token it cannot validate. This is a correctness bug, not a hardening item.

UnsignedToken::required_algorithm() already carries the constraint out of the token builder, and PgKeyRepository::active_signing_key(alg) already selects by algorithm — so the fix is either a Signer::sign_with(tenant, algorithm, typ, claims) on the port, or a direct call at the token endpoint that bypasses the convenience method. The port is shared domain surface, which is why the agent that found this did not change it.

Found by the ast-a05.4 agent, which built at_hash correctly and then noticed nothing could give it the right algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: A client registered for ES256 receives an ID token signed with ES256 and an at_hash computed with SHA-256; one registered for EdDSA gets EdDSA and SHA-512. A test registers a client for each algorithm in SigningAlgorithm::ALL and verifies the issued token against the registered algorithm.
notes: ADR-0003 pins EdDSA to Ed25519, which is what makes the at_hash pairing total: RFC 8037 §3.1 leaves the variant to the key subtype and RFC 8032 §5.1 makes Ed25519's hash SHA-512.
close_reason: Signer::sign now takes Option<SigningAlgorithm>; ID tokens are signed with the client's registered id_token_signed_response_alg and a tenant lacking the key is refused with DomainError::NoSigningKey. Commit 52f8f71 on worktree-agent-ad472e25831926ff9.

title: Interaction HTTP handlers and the PostgreSQL adapter
description: ast-2vk.1 landed the interaction engine — the id and its __Host- cookie, the CSRF token, the state machine, the templates and their escaping proofs. What is left is the wiring: GET/POST /interaction/{id}/{stage} handlers resuming through Interaction::resume (path id and cookie must both match) and rendering through Document; the store adapter against auth_requests keyed by interaction_id_hash; destroying the interaction and clearing the cookie on a browser mismatch; and the error page path with a correlation id logged beside the real reason.
acceptance_criteria: A request whose path id and cookie disagree gets the error page, the row is gone and the cookie is cleared. A POST without the issued CSRF token gets 403. Reloading a stage twice before deciding succeeds. An expired interaction is indistinguishable from an absent one to the browser.
notes: Blocked on the auth_requests.interaction_id_hash column requested from the ast-uwv.7 agent. Engine is in crates/web/src/{interaction,pages}.rs.
close_reason: Handlers and adapter merged; 15 new tests; full gate green. Credential verification is the typed UserAuthentication seam, owned by ast-2vk.5.

title: Per-tenant pairwise salt has no storage (blocks minting any subject)
description:
ast-2vk.6 landed derive_subject() and PgUserRepository::subject(), but both take the pairwise salt as an *argument* — nothing persists it and the baseline schema has no column for it. Until that exists there is no production path that mints a subject at all, so this blocks every flow that issues an id_token.

The salt is key material: it must be sealed under the existing Kek port exactly as signing keys are (a *_ciphertext column, see crates/store-pg/src/key_store.rs and 0001_baseline.sql signing_keys), not stored in plaintext. A leaked salt lets an attacker correlate every pairwise sub across every sector for that tenant, which is the entire property pairwise subjects exist to provide.

Note the rotation constraint recorded in docs/threat-model.md: the salt can never be rotated, because every derived sub is already stored and OIDC Core §8 says a Subject Identifier is never reassigned. Recovering from a leak means reissuing every identifier — a relying-party migration. Generate it once, at tenant creation.
acceptance_criteria: Migration adds an encrypted per-tenant salt column sealed under Kek; a tenant gets a salt at creation; derive_subject reads it from the store rather than taking it as an argument; a DB test proves the raw column is ciphertext and that the same (user, sector) yields a stable sub across processes.
notes: Reported by the ast-2vk.6 agent as out of scope (it was told not to write migrations). Depends on ast-mxc.3's Kek wiring, which has landed.
close_reason: Per-tenant pairwise salt now has storage: tenant_pairwise_salts, sealed under the Kek port, written once at tenant creation. derive_subject is a method on PairwiseSalt and PgUserRepository::subject reads the salt from the store rather than taking it as an argument. Rotation refused by an UPDATE trigger and by the absence of any mutator.

title: Strict CSP (nonce + strict-dynamic) & security headers on every HTML response
description:
Middleware sets per-response nonce and headers: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'nonce-{n}' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'nonce-{n}'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'self' {redirect-origin-when-form_post}; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: publickey-credentials-get=(self), publickey-credentials-create=(self)`, `Cache-Control: no-store` on interaction pages.

Spec: FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 (browser endpoints: HSTS, no CORS on authorization endpoint); RFC 9700 §4 (clickjacking, referrer leakage); CSP Level 3; RFC 6797 (HSTS).

Depends on: E01_04

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration test iterates every HTML route and asserts the header set; nonce differs per response and matches the one in the page.
- form_post page's `form-action` includes exactly the redirect_uri origin (E05_05).
- No `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` anywhere (grep test); CSP report-only endpoint optional for staging.
- Playwright run reports zero CSP violations across the no-JS and JS suites.
notes:
Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a22d4906e68a9bc89, commit 72a6a70. Left in progress deliberately, for two reasons: the Playwright acceptance criterion moved to ast-ndk.6 (blocked on ast-2vk.1), and the project rule in CONTRIBUTING.md says a citation is a claim a human still has to check — the clauses cited are RFC 9700 §4.16/§4.2.4/§4.3, CSP Level 3 §2.3.1/§6.4.2.2/§7.1/§8.2, FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3, RFC 8252 §7.3.

Shipped: crates/web/src/csp.rs (Nonce, Policy, FormActionOrigin), crates/web/src/document.rs (Document + middleware), crates/web/src/source_audit.rs (three whole-tree absence checks), crates/server/tests/browser_security.rs, fuzz/fuzz_targets/csp_form_action.rs, threat-model rows, and the layer wired into http::server::with_middleware.

Citation correction for the ticket text: FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 ('Requirements for endpoints used by web browsers') covers HSTS, BCP 195 cipher suites and 'shall not support CORS for the authorization endpoint'. It says nothing about CSP. The normative source for this story is RFC 9700 §4.16 ('Authorization servers MUST prevent clickjacking attacks' ... 'SHOULD also use Content Security Policy (CSP) level 2 or greater') plus §4.2.4 for Referrer-Policy and the no-third-party-resources rule.
close_reason: Merged to main, full gate green. Citations verified against the published texts: RFC 9700 §4.16 is Clickjacking (the ticket's FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 is browser-endpoint TLS/CORS and does not cover CSP); RFC 9700 §4.2.4 carries the third-party-resources rule; FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 items 6, 8 and 13 confirmed for client auth.

title: Refresh tokens: opaque, grant-bound, no rotation (FAPI 2.0), revocable
description:
Opaque ≥256-bit refresh tokens stored as SHA-256 digests with grant, client, scopes, absolute and idle expiry. No rotation by default; a time-boxed rotation mode exists only for migrations (FAPI Note 1) and offers the old token for retry within a grace window.

Spec: RFC 6749 §1.5, §6 (refresh request: grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, scope ⊆ original), §10.4; OIDC Core §12.1–12.3 (refresh: ID Token MAY be returned; `sub` MUST match; new nonce not required); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 9 ('shall not use refresh token rotation except in extraordinary circumstances'), Note 1, §6.1 (long-lived grants → short ATs + RTs); RFC 9449 §5 (refresh tokens for public clients bound to DPoP key; confidential clients: new AT bound to the proof key presented); RFC 9700 §4.14 (refresh token protection: sender-constrained or rotation — we use client authentication + optional key binding).

Depends on: E08_02, E07_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Refresh request requires client authentication and a DPoP proof; the new access token's `cnf.jkt` is the presented proof key; tenant option `bind_refresh_to_dpop_key` rejects a different key (`invalid_grant`).
- Requested `scope` ⊄ granted → `invalid_scope`; narrowing allowed; `openid` present → new ID token with same `sub` and `auth_time`.
- Same refresh token value returned unchanged (no rotation) by default; migration mode issues a new token and accepts the old one for `grace_seconds` (test both).
- Revoked grant/session-linked policy → `invalid_grant`; absolute lifetime and idle lifetime enforced; audit events on refresh.
- FAPI2 conformance refresh-token tests pass.
close_reason:
Le grant refresh_token existe de bout en bout : tokens opaques de 256 bits stockes en digest SHA-256, lies au grant, au client, aux scopes et a la cle DPoP, avec DEUX expirations distinctes — absolue figee, inactivite repoussee a l'usage. Pas de rotation par defaut (FAPI 2.0 SP 5.3.2.1 item 9), mode migration borne avec fenetre de grace.

L'ECART SIGNALE EST REFERME ET VERROUILLE : metadata.rs annoncait refresh_token alors que le endpoint repondait 501. Le handler est enregistre, et un test nomme discovery_advertises_the_grant_this_file_implements empeche l'ecart de reapparaitre — mieux que la correction ponctuelle demandee.

http::issuance (nouveau) partage auth_time, sid et claims entre authorization_code et refresh_token pour qu'ils ne puissent pas diverger.

BUG REEL ATTRAPE PAR UN TEST : redeem ecrivait idle_expires_at sans le plafonner a absolute_expires_at, violant le CHECK et cassant TOUT refresh en fin de vie. Corrige par un least(...). Le test de plan confirme une lecture par refresh_tokens_pkey sans Seq Scan sur 5000 tokens.

LES DEUX MODES testes : non-rotation (meme token, presentable deux fois) et migration (nouveau token, l'ancien valable dans la grace et plus au-dela, remplacant redeemable).

Dependance retiree au passage : ast-a05.5 etait declare bloque par ast-uwv.3 (memoire de consentement), alors que celle-ci ne ferme qu'un RESIDU documente au threat model — un grant offline_access dont la session a ete purgee ne peut plus etre rafraichi faute d'auth_time. Ce n'est pas un bloqueur du grant.

116/116, clippy propre sans #[allow], 42 cibles fuzz. Verifie apres merge : workspace compile, doc -D warnings a 0, gate fuzz verte, suite navigateur 19/19. Merge 57e4b26.

title: DPoP (RFC 9449): proof validation, jkt binding, nonce, `dpop_jkt` in PAR, metadata
description:
Proof validation middleware for token, PAR (dpop_jkt correlation), UserInfo, introspection (optional), grant-management, SSF-management and AuthZEN endpoints. Replay store in PostgreSQL keyed by (tenant, jkt, jti) with TTL = iat window.

Spec: RFC 9449 §4.1 (`DPoP` header), §4.2 (proof JWT: typ dpop+jwt, alg asymmetric ≠ none, jwk public key; claims jti, htm, htu, iat, nonce, ath), §4.3 (checking: exactly one header; parse; typ; alg; signature with jwk; jti replay; htm/htu match; iat window; nonce), §5 (token request: `token_type: DPoP`; error `invalid_dpop_proof`), §6.1 (`cnf.jkt` = JWK thumbprint RFC 7638), §8 (AS-provided nonce: `use_dpop_nonce` 400 + `DPoP-Nonce` header), §10.1 (`dpop_jkt` authorization request parameter), §10.2 (in PAR), §11 (`dpop_signing_alg_values_supported`), §12 (`dpop_bound_access_tokens`), §13 (security: htu normalisation, replay); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 items 4–5 (sender-constrained via DPoP), 10 (nonce MAY), 12 (must support code binding to DPoP key), 13 (skew).

Depends on: E02_04, E08_01, E02_06

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two `DPoP` headers → `invalid_dpop_proof`/`invalid_request`; missing `typ`/wrong `typ`, `alg` outside {ES256, EdDSA, PS256}, symmetric alg, `jwk` containing private members → `invalid_dpop_proof`.
- `htm` must equal the request method; `htu` compared after normalising scheme/host case and stripping query/fragment; mismatch → `invalid_dpop_proof`.
- `iat` outside [now−300 s, now+10 s] → reject (window configurable ≤ 60 s future); `jti` replay → reject.
- Tenant `dpop_nonce=required`: missing/stale nonce → 400 `use_dpop_nonce` + fresh `DPoP-Nonce`; nonces are HMAC-derived, valid 5 min, no storage.
- `dpop_jkt` accepted in PAR and stored on the code; token request proof key must match (E08_02).
- Issued tokens: `token_type: "DPoP"`, `cnf.jkt` = RFC 7638 thumbprint; metadata `dpop_signing_alg_values_supported`.
- Fuzz target `dpop_proof`; FAPI2 conformance DPoP tests pass; test vectors from RFC 9449 §4.2 reproduced.
notes:
Implemented on branch worktree-agent-ad795715ca61bac04.

Built: crates/jose/src/dpop.rs (proof checking, htu normalisation, HMAC-derived nonces, RFC 9449 s10 key binding), crates/server/src/http/dpop.rs (header extraction, endpoint URL, replay claim, use_dpop_nonce handshake), fuzz/fuzz_targets/dpop_proof.rs. dpop_signing_alg_values_supported was already in metadata.rs; added a test naming RFC 9449 s5.1 and a cross-crate test that every advertised algorithm actually verifies.

NOT closed: the project DoD says generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections. The endpoint is also not mounted — see ast-a05.10.

Citation corrections found while implementing, verified against the published RFC: dpop_jkt is s10 (not s10.1/s10.2); dpop_signing_alg_values_supported is s5.1 (not s11); dpop_bound_access_tokens is s5.2 (not s12); security considerations are s11 and proof replay s11.1 (not s13); htu normalisation guidance is the last paragraph of s4.3, citing RFC 3986 s6.2.2/s6.2.3. FAPI 2.0 SP s5.3.2.1 items 4, 5, 10, 12 and 13 in this ticket are all correct as written. See ast-64u.
close_reason: Merged and mounted; full gate green.

title: JWT access token profile (RFC 9068, `at+jwt`, always audience- and sender-bound)
description:
Signed (EdDSA default) self-contained access tokens; opaque reference tokens are out of scope (KISS). Lifetime default 300 s, tenant/resource cap 900 s.

Spec: RFC 9068 §2.1 (header `typ: at+jwt`), §2.2 (claims iss, exp, aud, sub, client_id, iat, jti REQUIRED), §2.2.1 (auth_time, acr, amr), §2.2.3 (scope, groups/roles/entitlements), §4 (validation rules for RS — informs tests), §5 (security: aud restriction, no sensitive data); RFC 9449 §6.1 (`cnf.jkt`); RFC 8705 §3 (`cnf.x5t#S256`); RFC 8693 §4.1 (`act`); RFC 9396 §8.1 (`authorization_details`); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 4 (only sender-constrained access tokens), item 14 (least privilege), §6.1 (short-lived access tokens), §5.4.1.

Depends on: E02_01, E07_02

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Header `{alg, kid, typ: "at+jwt"}`; claims `iss`, `sub` (user sub or `client_id` for client_credentials), `aud` (non-empty; resource identifiers), `client_id`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti` (≥128 bits), `scope`, `cnf` (`jkt` or `x5t#S256` — REQUIRED, a token without `cnf` cannot be built), optional `auth_time`/`acr`/`amr`, `authorization_details`, `act`, `grant_id` (private claim, tenant option).
- `exp - iat` ≤ 900 s enforced by the builder; ID-token-only claims (nonce, at_hash) never appear; no PII beyond `sub` unless resource policy opts in.
- Serialised token ≤ 4 KiB by default (guard); property test on builder invariants.
- Verification helper for resource servers (`asterius-rs` crate or docs) implements RFC 9068 §4 and DPoP §7 checks — used by UserInfo (E09_03) and introspection (E09_01).
close_reason: Closed

title: ID Token issuance (claims, nonce, auth_time, acr/amr, sid, at_hash, pairwise sub)
description:
Built after grant/claims resolution (E09_04). Signed with the client's `id_token_signed_response_alg` (default EdDSA). Explicit `typ: JWT` header.

Spec: OIDC Core §2 (ID Token claims: iss, sub, aud, exp, iat REQUIRED; auth_time, nonce, acr, amr, azp), §3.1.3.6 (ID Token from token endpoint; at_hash OPTIONAL in code flow), §3.1.3.7 (validation rules the client applies — drive our tests), §5.4/§5.5 (claims in the ID Token via scopes/`claims`), §10.1 (signing; `alg` per `id_token_signed_response_alg`; `none` forbidden here), §15.1 (mandatory to implement), §8.1 (pairwise sub); Back-Channel Logout §2.3 (remembering logged-in RPs) and §2.4 (`sid` in ID Token and Logout Token).

Depends on: E02_01, E09_04

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Claims: `iss` = tenant issuer, `sub` (public/pairwise per client), `aud` = client_id string, `exp` (default 300 s), `iat`, `auth_time` (always), `nonce` echoed byte-exact when supplied, `acr`, `amr`, `azp` = client_id, `sid`, `at_hash` (present for code flow as a defensive extra), plus requested claims.
- Signature alg ∈ allow-list; `none` and HS* impossible; `kid` present; verifies against JWKS in a test using an independent JWT library.
- Refresh-token-issued ID tokens carry the same `sub`/`auth_time` (Core §12.2) and no `nonce` unless original.
- Conformance `oidcc` ID-token checks (as run inside the FAPI2 plan) pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Token endpoint framework & client-authentication dispatch
description:
One handler that authenticates the client (E03_02/E03_03), validates the DPoP proof when present (E08_06), parses `grant_type` and dispatches to grant handlers enabled by feature flags and the client's `grant_types`.

Spec: RFC 6749 §3.2 (token endpoint: POST, TLS, client auth), §3.2.1, §4.1.3, §5.1 (success: `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`), §5.2 (errors invalid_request, invalid_client (401 + WWW-Authenticate when header auth attempted), invalid_grant, unauthorized_client, unsupported_grant_type, invalid_scope); OIDC Core §3.1.3 (token endpoint), §3.1.3.4 (token error response); RFC 6750 §3.

Depends on: E03_02, E01_04

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Non-POST or non-`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` → 400 `invalid_request`; duplicate parameter → `invalid_request` (RFC 6749 §3.2: 'Request and response parameters MUST NOT be included more than once').
- Grant type not enabled for the client → `unauthorized_client`; unknown → `unsupported_grant_type`.
- Every success response has `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`; JSON errors with `error`, optional `error_description` (ASCII-only), never stack traces.
- Parsing is total (never panics) — fuzz target `token_form`; property test that unknown parameters are ignored.
close_reason: Merged to main; full gate green including the rebuilt baseline.

title: authorization_code grant (PKCE, redirect_uri, DPoP-key binding, replay)
description:
Redeem a code for tokens. All bindings recorded at issuance (E05_04) are checked here.

Spec: RFC 6749 §4.1.3 (grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri REQUIRED if included in the authorization request, client_id), §4.1.4; OIDC Core §3.1.3.1 (token request), §3.1.3.2 (validation: authenticate client, code issued to this client, code not used, redirect_uri identical), §3.1.3.3 (successful response: access_token, token_type, refresh_token, expires_in, id_token); RFC 7636 §4.6; RFC 9449 §10 ('Authorization Code Binding to DPoP Key': `dpop_jkt` must match the proof key at the token endpoint); RFC 8707 §2.2; FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 12, §5.3.2.2 item 9.

Depends on: E08_01, E05_04, E05_03, E08_03, E08_04, E08_06

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Code unknown/expired/other client → `invalid_grant`; `redirect_uri` not byte-identical to the PAR value → `invalid_grant`.
- PKCE verifier mismatch → `invalid_grant`; code bound to `dpop_jkt` and proof thumbprint differs or proof absent → `invalid_grant`; code issued without `dpop_jkt` still requires a DPoP proof (all ATs sender-constrained).
- Second use → `invalid_grant` and revocation of the tokens from the first use (E05_04).
- Response: `access_token` (E08_03), `token_type: "DPoP"` (or `Bearer` only for mTLS-bound tokens), `expires_in`, `id_token` when `openid` scope (E08_04), `refresh_token` per E08_05, `scope` when it differs from the request, `authorization_details` when RAR, `grant_id` when Grant Management.
- FAPI2 conformance token-endpoint tests pass.
notes:
Implemented and committed (ac61780). crates/server/src/http/authorization_code.rs, wired per-request in protocol.rs::token_endpoint; 8 spec-derived tests in crates/server/tests/authorization_code.rs, all passing against PostgreSQL. Full CI gate set green (fmt, clippy -D warnings, layering, no-unsafe, fuzz coverage, 1079 tests, doctests, sqlx prepare --check, rustdoc, cargo-deny).

DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED. Three things stand between this and done:

1. The project DoD says 'generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections'. Nobody has. The sections to read against the implementation are RFC 6749 §4.1.3-§4.1.4, OIDC Core §3.1.3.1-§3.1.3.3 and §3.1.3.6, RFC 7636 §4.6, RFC 9449 §10, and FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 12 / §5.3.2.2 item 9.
2. 'FAPI2 conformance token-endpoint tests pass' cannot be evaluated: the harness is ast-83p.8, still open.
3. Three response members in the acceptance criteria belong to beads that are not built: refresh_token (ast-a05.5), authorization_details (ast-gxh.6), grant_id (Grant Management). The response carries access_token, token_type=DPoP, expires_in, scope, and id_token when the grant has openid.

Delivered beyond the original scope, because nothing could issue a token without it: a per-tenant default_resource (RFC 9068 §3) on the tenants table, in config, and in asterius.example.toml. New threat-model row covering it.

sid is omitted on purpose — see ast-o4u.5, which now blocks ast-o4u.1.

comments.author: Quentin RODIC
comments.text:
RÉOUVERTURE PARTIELLE DE MON AUDIT. J'ai fermé ce ticket aujourd'hui sur une lecture de code, en constatant la PRÉSENCE de check_dpop sans vérifier son COMPORTEMENT. Son critère d'acceptation disait pourtant : « code bound to dpop_jkt and proof thumbprint differs or proof absent → invalid_grant ».

La suite de conformance OIDF, montée le même jour par ast-83p.8, a trouvé que ce critère N'EST PAS tenu : un dpop_jkt annoncé à l'autorisation et une preuve signée par une autre clé donnent un 200. Voir ast-36g (P0).

Le ticket reste fermé — le grant existe et ses autres critères tiennent — mais l'audit qui l'a fermé était insuffisant sur ce point précis, et c'est consigné ici pour que personne ne s'y fie.

title: Grant model & persistence (every token links to a revocable grant)
description:
grants row: tenant, client, user (null for client_credentials), scopes, claims,
authorization_details, resources, status (pending|active|revoked|expired),
created_at, last_updated_at, expires_at, updated_by. Codes, refresh tokens,
access-token jti and device/CIBA requests reference grant_id.

Spec: Grant Management for OAuth 2.0 (oauth-v2-grant-management-03, Implementer's
Draft 1, 9 May 2023) §5.6 'Lifecycle of the grant' (active once tokens claimed;
delete unclaimed after timeout; AS may modify) — verified against the published
text; FAPI 2.0 Security Profile (Final, 22 February 2025) §6.8 'Key Compromise'
item 4, 'Credential linking': "When multiple credentials are issued as part of the
same authorization, it is recommended that their relationship be explicitly
established and recorded. This way, if one credential in a linked set is
compromised, all related credentials can be revoked."

CITATION CORRECTION (verified 2026-09-08 against the published Final text): this
ticket previously cited FAPI 2.0 SP §6.7 item 4. §6.7 is 'Client Impersonating
Resource Owner' and carries no numbered list at all; credential linking is §6.8
item 4. docs/BACKLOG.md already said §6.8. Beads still carrying the wrong §6.7:
ast-83p.11, ast-lh3.9, ast-f7m.7, ast-mxc.3, ast-lh3.1 (that last one cites §6.6
for client impersonation, which is 'Incomplete or incorrect implementations' — the
impersonation section is §6.7).

Depends on: E01_03, E03_01, E06_06

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes;
fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no
new unsafe; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the
cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every token issuance path (code, refresh, client_credentials, token exchange, device, CIBA) requires a `grant_id` (compile-time non-optional).
- Revoking a grant marks refresh tokens revoked and inserts their access-token jti into the denylist until `exp` (introspection returns `active:false`).
- Unclaimed grants (no token issued) are garbage-collected after tenant timeout.
- Single active default grant per (client,user) unless Grant Management `create` action is used (E07_04) — concurrent grants supported by schema.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a2d1c2e396c4a56e9. Domain: crates/domain/src/entities/grant.rs (Grant, GrantStatus, RevocationReason, GrantRecord validator, ClaimedGrant, LiveAccessToken). Adapter: crates/store-pg/src/grants.rs (PgGrantRepository: create/find/list_for_subject/claim/revoke/purge_unclaimed, Revocation). Fuzz: fuzz/fuzz_targets/grant_record.rs. 21 unit tests + 8 db_test cases. Two acceptance criteria are only partly met by the baseline schema and are carried by ast-uwv.7: there is no claimed_at column (pending/active is derived) and no record of issued access tokens (revoke takes the live set as a required parameter). Also: no status column or check constraint exists on grants, so status is computed by Grant::status(now) rather than stored; no updated_by column (needed by ast-uwv.5).
close_reason: Grant entity, PgGrantRepository, atomic revocation cascade, per-tenant GC and fuzz target landed; schema gaps carried by ast-uwv.7

title: Consent screen (client identity, scopes, claims, RAR, resources; no JS)
description:
SSR consent page listing client name/URI (text only; logo only if uploaded to the IdP), scopes with tenant descriptions, requested claims, RAR items rendered by type template, target resources, offline access, and Approve/Deny. Deny is a first-class outcome.

Spec: OIDC Core §3.1.2.4 (obtain end-user consent/authorization); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 item 13 (provide all information for an informed decision: client identity and scope), §7 (privacy: client misidentification, insufficient understanding, inadequate choice); RFC 9396 §2 (render authorization details).

Depends on: E06_01, E06_02

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Page shows `client_name` and the redirect target's host; no remote assets are loaded (CSP `img-src 'self' data:`).
- Approve/Deny are plain form POSTs with CSRF; Deny → `access_denied` redirect (E05_04).
- Consent decision (scopes/claims/details actually granted, which may be a subset when tenant allows partial consent) is recorded on the grant with timestamp and audit event.
- Snapshot tests for the page in en/fr and for RAR rendering; no-JS Playwright test.
close_reason: Consent screen, decision model and handler merged; deny is first-class and narrowing is recorded. Per-tenant scope wording (ast-ndk.2) and the signed-in display name (ast-2vk.8) are recorded as residuals.

title: User & issuer-agnostic claims model (public/pairwise subjects)
description:
`users` (stable `sub`, status, tenant), `identifiers` (email/phone with `verified`), `claims` JSONB where every claim carries `value`, `source` (local|admin|import|<issuer>) and `verified_at` so future aggregated/verified claims fit without a schema change. Pairwise `sub` = base64url(SHA-256(sector || local_sub || tenant_salt)).

Spec: OIDC Core §5.1 (standard claims), §5.7 (claim stability and uniqueness: sub locally unique, never reassigned), §8 (subject identifier types public/pairwise), §8.1 (pairwise algorithm: sector identifier from `sector_identifier_uri` host or redirect_uri host; MUST NOT be reversible; salt), §5.6.2 (aggregated/distributed claims — schema readiness only); OIDC Registration §5 (sector_identifier_uri validation).

Depends on: E01_03, E01_10

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- `sub` is never reused after deletion (tombstone table + test).
- Pairwise: two clients with different sectors get different `sub`; same sector → same `sub`; salt rotation is impossible by design (documented).
- `sector_identifier_uri` fetched over https at registration time (OIDC Registration §5), must list all `redirect_uris` (and `jwks_uri`/`backchannel_client_notification_endpoint` for CIBA clients) else `invalid_client_metadata`.
- Standard claims (`name`, `email`, `email_verified`, `phone_number`, `address`, `locale`, `zoneinfo`, `updated_at` …) round-trip through the claims service with language tags (`name#ja-Kana-JP`).
- Admin CRUD for users and identifiers; account states active/disabled/locked drive `login_required`/error handling.
close_reason: Implemented in worktree, merged to main, full gate green.

title: Passkey authentication (discoverable credentials, conditional UI as enhancement)
description:
Username-less flow first (discoverable credential), username-first fallback. Conditional UI (autofill) is progressive enhancement only.

Spec: WebAuthn L3 §7.2 (verifying an authentication assertion: challenge, origin, rpIdHash, UP/UV flags, sign count); RFC 8176 (`amr` values: `hwk`, `swk`, `user`, `pin`); OIDC Core §2 (acr, amr, auth_time).

Depends on: E06_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Assertion validated per §7.2; sign-count regression flagged in audit and (policy) blocks the credential.
- `amr` set to [`hwk`|`swk`, `user`] (+`pin` when UV via PIN is reported) and `acr` mapped by tenant policy (E06_07); `auth_time` updated.
- Challenge single-use; failed attempts rate-limited per IP and per user (E06_09).
- No-JS fallback path exists; JS-enabled path adds passkeys and autofill.
- Integration test with a virtual authenticator (Playwright CDP) covers registration + login.
close_reason:
WebAuthn section 7.2 implemente dans asterius-webauthn::assertion : client data, en-tete d'authenticator data partage avec 7.1, signature verifiee via aws-lc-rs — aucune nouvelle bibliotheque crypto, ADR-0007 respectee. Deux routes sous l'interaction transforment une assertion verifiee en session (amr swk+user, jamais pin faute de uvm), allowCredentials OMIS puisque le credential est decouvrable et qu'aucun username n'est echange.

LE COMPTEUR DE SIGNATURE, coeur du ticket, est traite selon la spec et non selon l'intuition — section 7.2 etape 21, applique APRES la verification de signature. Trois cas : les deux a zero = authentificateur qui ne compte pas (section 6.1.1, cas legitime des passkeys synchronisees) donc accepte sans rien ecrire ; compteur avance = stocke ; REGRESSION = credential desactive et evenement auth.failed portant les deux valeurs, le navigateur recevant le meme refus generique. C'est la protection anti-clonage qui existait sur le papier depuis ast-2vk.15 et n'etait pas branchee.

Refus unique et identique pour credential inconnu, bloque, mauvaise origine, mauvais RP ID, UV manquant, handle etranger et compte desactive.

Challenge lie a l'INTERACTION (auth_requests.passkey_challenge, TTL 5 min), depense par le meme update-returning-previous que passkey_enrolments.

Conditional UI livree comme AMELIORATION : bouton hidden revele par le script, motif ast-ndk.7 justifie parce qu'ici le bouton EST le script ; le formulaire mot de passe reste le mecanisme sans script.

CORRIGE EN PASSANT : le test retention a_sweep_removes_the_expired_row_from_every_swept_table echouait sur main depuis ast-2vk.15 ; passkey_enrolments est desormais balaye avant sessions pour que ses lignes soient rapportees par sa propre regle plutot que de disparaitre par la cascade.

Dependance corrigee : ast-2vk.4 etait declare dependant d'ast-2vk.3 alors qu'il lui fallait la PLOMBERIE d'ast-2vk.15, fermee — pas la page compte qui est tout ce qui reste au parent.

155 puis 73 tests, clippy et rustdoc -D warnings propres. Verifie apres merge : 14/14 sur retention, suite navigateur 17/17. Merge 9613e93.

title: Server-side session management (`sid`, lifetimes, participating clients)
description:
Sessions in PostgreSQL keyed by an opaque id (≥128 bits, hashed at rest) carried by `__Host-asterius_session`. Tracks user, auth_time, acr/amr, idle/absolute expiry, participating clients (for back-channel logout) and device summary.

Spec: OIDC Core §3.1.2.3; OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout §2.1 (`backchannel_logout_session_supported`), §2.4 (`sid` claim in ID Token and Logout Token — section numbers as in the Final spec); OWASP ASVS V3 (session lifetime, rotation).

Depends on: E01_03, E06_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Session id rotated on login and on step-up; old id invalid immediately (test).
- Idle timeout and absolute lifetime per tenant; expired session → `login_required` for prompt=none.
- ID tokens carry `sid`; the session records every client that received an ID token in it.
- Revoke by id/user/admin; revoked session cannot be used for prompt=none; audit event and CAEP hook (E12_08).
close_reason: Session model, port and PostgreSQL adapter merged; 24 tests including rotation atomicity and revoke-by-user. Back-channel logout participants recorded.

title: Passkey registration (WebAuthn L3 via webauthn-rs)
description:
RP ID = tenant host (configurable subdomain policy). Discoverable credentials requested, user verification required by default, attestation `none` unless tenant enables enterprise attestation with an AAGUID allowlist.

Spec: W3C WebAuthn Level 3 §7.1 (registering a new credential: challenge, origin, RP ID, UV, attestation); FIDO Alliance passkey guidance (discoverable credentials).

Depends on: E06_02, E06_06

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Challenge ≥ 16 bytes, single-use, ≤ 5 min TTL, bound to the session/interaction.
- Origin and RP ID verified exactly; UV flag required when policy `uv=required`; failing either → registration rejected with generic error.
- Credential id uniqueness enforced across the tenant; backup-eligible/backup-state flags and sign count stored; user can name/rename/delete passkeys (account page E06_08).
- Without JavaScript the page shows the password/alternative path and an explanation (no dead end).
- Audit event + CAEP `credential-change` (create) emitted (E12_08).
notes:
Ceremony verification is DONE and committed (c87aca3): crates/webauthn implements WebAuthn L3 §7.1 for attestation none, with 21 spec-derived tests and 4 fuzz targets. ADR-0007 records why webauthn-rs could not be used.

NOT done — the bead's remaining acceptance criteria are all plumbing, split out because none of it had any scaffolding:
- ast-2vk.15 (P0): routes, challenge store (>=16 bytes, single-use, <=5 min, bound to the interaction), credential writes, the session-cookie reader that would tell us who is registering, schema gaps, tenant RP-ID/origin/uv policy.
- ast-ndk.7 (P1): the ceremony script, the source_audit exemption it needs, and the no-JS fallback.
- ast-2vk.16 (P1): the audit event and CAEP credential-change.

Also unverified: the DoD's 'a human has read the cited spec sections'. The sections to read against crates/webauthn are WebAuthn L3 §7.1 (steps 5-22), §6.1, §6.5.2, §8.7 and RFC 9052 §7 / RFC 8230 §4 for the COSE keys.
close_reason: Clos par le propriétaire (2026-09-10). Cérémonie §7.1 dans crates/webauthn (c87aca3, 21 tests spec, 4 cibles fuzz, ADR-0007) ; plomberie par ast-2vk.15 (routes /passkeys, challenge 32 o usage unique TTL 5 min lié à la session, unicité tenant, flags backup et compteur, audit, refus générique) ; page et chemin sans JS par ast-ndk.7. Reste hors de ce ticket : page compte lister/renommer/supprimer -> ast-2vk.8 ; assertion et lecture du compteur -> ast-2vk.4 ; RP ID par tenant pour custom_host hors domaine et uv relaxable par tenant -> consignés dans docs/threat-model.md.

comments.author: Quentin RODIC
comments.text:
La PLOMBERIE est livrée par ast-2vk.15 (merge 6c6fa49) : routes GET /passkeys et POST /passkeys/{options,finish}, table passkey_enrolments (challenge 32 o, usage unique, TTL 5 min, lié à la session), écriture du credential avec unicité tenant, audit, refus générique. La page passkey.html d'ast-ndk.7 est désormais atteignable et la suite navigateur passe 14/14 sans skip.

Critères du parent DÉJÀ TENUS : challenge ≥ 16 octets à usage unique et TTL ≤ 5 min lié à la session ; origine et RP ID vérifiés exactement, UV requis, échec -> erreur générique ; unicité du credential id à l'échelle du tenant ; backup-eligible/backup-state et compteur de signature stockés ; chemin sans JavaScript non bloquant.

CE QUI RESTE À CE TICKET : la page compte (lister, renommer, supprimer un passkey — 'label' reste NULL et next_href/password_href pointent sur /passkeys faute de destination), soit E06_08.

Points connexes ouverts : ast-2vk.4 (assertion — le compteur de signature est stocké mais rien ne le lit encore), RP ID par tenant pour un custom_host hors du domaine de l'issuer, et uv=required relaxable par tenant. Ces trois lacunes sont documentées dans le tableau de docs/threat-model.md avec quatre nouvelles lignes de menaces.

title: Interaction engine & SSR page framework (CSRF, CSP nonce, no-JS)
description:
An `Interaction` (id ≥128 bits, bound to the PAR request and to a `__Host-asterius_ix` cookie) drives a state machine login → step-up → consent → response. askama templates with autoescape; per-response CSP nonce; synchroniser CSRF token per form; every page usable without JavaScript.

Spec: OIDC Core §3.1.2.3 (authorization server authenticates end-user; MUST NOT interact if prompt=none), §3.1.2.4; FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 (browser endpoints), §6.5 (browser-swapping: keep authorization response confidential); RFC 9700 §4 (clickjacking and open-redirector countermeasures — exact section number from memory, verify).

Depends on: E01_04, E01_10, E15_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Interaction id in path + `__Host-` cookie (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) must both match; mismatch → error page, interaction invalidated.
- Every POST form carries a CSRF token validated with `ct_eq`; missing/invalid → 403 page.
- Playwright no-JS test completes login (password) → consent → code redirect.
- Template snapshot tests prove untrusted values (client_name, state, login_hint) are escaped; no template uses `|safe` on request data.
- Error pages show a correlation id and a generic message; never echo `error_description` from request parameters.
close_reason: Interaction engine, templates and source audits landed; HTTP handlers and adapter split to ast-2vk.13 (done) and the browser sweep to ast-2vk.14 (open, no Playwright harness exists).

title: response_mode=form_post (server-rendered auto-submit, works without JavaScript)
description:
Template renders a hidden form with `code`, `state`, `iss`; a nonce-CSP script auto-submits; `<noscript>` shows a Continue button. Only `query` and `form_post` are accepted for `response_type=code`.

Spec: OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode §2 (HTML form POST to redirect_uri with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body containing all response parameters; MUST NOT be cached); OAuth 2.0 Multiple Response Type Encoding Practices §2.1 (`response_mode`); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 (browser endpoints).

Depends on: E05_04, E15_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- `response_mode=form_post` → 200 HTML, `Cache-Control: no-store`, form `method=post` `action` = exact redirect_uri, hidden inputs escaped; auto-submit script carries the per-response CSP nonce; page works with JS disabled (Playwright no-JS test submits via button).
- `response_mode=fragment` or unknown → `invalid_request` at PAR (documented interop note).
- Error responses honour form_post too.
- CSP `form-action` allows exactly the redirect_uri origin for this response.
notes:
From ast-ndk.3 (CSP): the form-action seam is built. Take the client's origin through asterius_web::csp::FormActionOrigin::parse and hand it to Document::with_form_post_to; the middleware renders 'form-action self <origin>' and nothing else can widen the policy.

One constraint that falls out of the CSP grammar, not out of this implementation: CSP Level 3 §2.3.1 defines host-char as ALPHA / DIGIT / '-', so an IPv6 literal host ('[::1]') cannot be written as a host-source at all. FormActionOrigin therefore refuses it. If a client ever registers an IPv6-literal redirect_uri, form_post to it cannot be expressed as a policy — decide then whether to refuse response_mode=form_post for that client (recommended) or to serve the page under a policy that would block its own submission. https and the RFC 8252 §7.3 127.0.0.1 loopback are both accepted.
close_reason:
ResponseMode (query | form_post) est validé au PAR et stocké avec la requête ; complete() branche dessus et rend form_post.html — action = le redirect_uri exact via AuthorizationResponse::form_action, entrées cachées échappées par askama, form-action 'self' plus l'origine du redirect_uri validé, no-store par le middleware.

La contradiction apparente du ticket — auto-soumission ET fonctionnement sans script — est résolue par INVERSION du motif passkey : le bouton submit est réel, visible et jamais désactivé, c'est LUI le mécanisme, et le script noncé (une ligne, zéro interpolation) se contente de le presser ; le <noscript> explique l'attente. Là où ast-ndk.7 cachait un bouton révélé par le script, ici le bouton est le chemin nominal.

Les réponses d'erreur (access_denied) passent par la même page — 3e critère, le plus facile à oublier. fragment et valeur inconnue -> invalid_request au PAR, avec note d'interopérabilité. Cas trouvé par le worker : un form_post vers un callback qu'aucune CSP ne sait nommer (littéral IPv6) est refusé AU PAR plutôt que servi, ce qui évite de rendre une page dont la soumission serait bloquée.

Seconde entrée dans SCRIPTED_TEMPLATES, discipline respectée : nommée, justifiée, un seul bloc inline porteur du nonce.

Nouveau fuzz target response_mode. 179/179 en tests ciblés, clippy workspace propre, rustdoc -D warnings propre, check-no-unsafe et check-layering OK. Suite Playwright : 12 passés / 2 skipped, le fixme de form-post.spec.ts est RETIRÉ et le test passe dans les deux projets — no-js presse le bouton, js n'appuie sur rien et arrive quand même. Vérifié après merge : 38 parsers, 38 [[bin]], workspace compile. Merge c486bf9.

comments.text: refuse response_mode=form_post for that client

title: PKCE S256 enforcement (no plain, no missing)
description:
Validation at PAR (challenge present, method S256, well-formed) and at the token endpoint (verifier present, S256 match, constant-time).

Spec: RFC 7636 §4.1 (verifier 43–128 unreserved chars), §4.2 (S256 = BASE64URL(SHA256(ASCII(verifier)))), §4.3 (client sends challenge), §4.4 (server associates challenge with code), §4.5 (client sends verifier), §4.6 (server verifies), §7.2 (entropy); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 item 5 ('shall require PKCE with S256'); RFC 9700 §4.8 (PKCE downgrade attack: reject token requests without verifier when challenge was present, and never accept codes issued without PKCE).

Depends on: E02_06

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- PAR without `code_challenge` or with `code_challenge_method` absent/`plain` → `invalid_request`.
- `code_challenge` not 43 chars base64url → `invalid_request`; token request `code_verifier` outside 43–128 unreserved chars → `invalid_grant`.
- Verifier/challenge mismatch → `invalid_grant`, code consumed and any tokens from that code revoked.
- Property test: for random verifiers, S256(verifier) matches; comparison uses `ct_eq`.
- Fuzz target `pkce`.
close_reason: Implemented in worktree, merged to main, full gate green.

title: Authorization response: code issuance (≤60 s, single-use, replay revocation) with `iss`
description:
After consent, mint an authorization code bound to client_id, redirect_uri, scope, nonce, PKCE challenge, `dpop_jkt`, resources, authorization_details, session id, auth_time, acr; persist hash; redirect via query or form_post.

Spec: OIDC Core §3.1.2.5 (successful authentication response: code, state), §3.1.2.6 (error response); RFC 6749 §4.1.2 (code lifetime SHOULD be short, MUST NOT be used more than once; on reuse 'SHOULD revoke all tokens previously issued based on that authorization code'), §4.1.2.1; RFC 9207 §2 (`iss` parameter MUST be included in successful and error responses when supported); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 item 7 (`iss` per RFC 9207), item 9 (reject previously used code), items 10–11 (no 307; 303), Note 1.

Depends on: E05_02, E06_02, E07_01

acceptance_criteria:
- Code is ≥128 bits random, stored as SHA-256, `expires_at` ≤ 60 s from issuance (tenant-configurable, hard cap 60).

title: Pushed Authorization Request endpoint (RFC 9126)
description:
Validates the whole authorization request at push time with the same rules as E05_02, stores it keyed by a ≥128-bit reference bound to the client, and returns the `request_uri`.

Spec: RFC 9126 §2.1 (request: client auth, all authorization parameters, `request_uri` MUST NOT be present), §2.2 (201 with `request_uri` urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri:… and `expires_in`), §2.3 (errors incl. `invalid_request`, `invalid_client` 401), §2.4 (redirect URI management), §7.1 (request_uri guessing), §7.3 (replay); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 items 2–4 (support client-authenticated PAR; reject requests without PAR; reject PAR without client auth), 6 (`redirect_uri` required in PAR), 12 (`expires_in` < 600 s), Note 3 (enforce one-time use at authorization, not page load).

Depends on: E03_02, E03_07, E05_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unauthenticated PAR → 401 `invalid_client`; PAR body containing `request_uri` → 400 `invalid_request`.

- `request_uri` of client A presented by client B at `/authorize` → error page (no redirect); expired → error page.
- One-time use is consumed when the user completes authorization/denial, not when the page is loaded (test: reload authorization page twice before consenting succeeds; replay after consent fails).

title: Authorization endpoint: PAR-only request handling & interaction hand-off
description:
`GET|POST /t/{tenant}/authorize?client_id&request_uri` loads the pushed request, re-checks binding, creates an interaction (E06_01) and redirects (303) to the login/consent pages. Pure-OAuth requests (no `openid` scope) are allowed and yield no ID token.

Spec: OIDC Core §3.1.2.1 (authentication request parameters; GET or POST; scope openid), §3.1.2.2 (request validation: 'MUST validate all OAuth 2.0 parameters'; 'MUST verify that a scope parameter is present and contains the openid scope value' for OIDC; ignore unrecognised parameters), §3.1.2.6 (error response); RFC 6749 §4.1.1, §4.1.2.1 (if redirect URI/client_id invalid: 'MUST NOT automatically redirect'); RFC 9126 §4 (client_id + request_uri at authorization endpoint); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 item 1 (`response_type` = `code`), item 3 (reject non-PAR), item 14 (nonce up to 64 chars).

Depends on: E05_01, E06_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Request without `request_uri` or with any other parameter than `client_id`/`request_uri` → rendered error page `invalid_request` (never a redirect, since the redirect_uri is untrusted).
- `client_id` mismatch with the pushed request's client → error page; expired/unknown/consumed `request_uri` → error page.
- Errors detectable only after the pushed request is trusted (e.g., `login_required`) are redirected to the pushed `redirect_uri` with `error`, `error_description`, `state`, `iss` (RFC 9207).
- `nonce` longer than 64 chars → `invalid_request`; unknown parameters ignored (test with 100 random params).
- `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response; interaction id is unguessable (≥128 bits) and bound to a `__Host-` cookie.
- FAPI2 conformance authorization endpoint tests pass; fuzz target `authorize_query`.
notes:
From ast-gxh.1: the PAR side is done and the storage guarantees are proven at the repository level (peek does not spend; 16 concurrent consumers yield exactly one winner; cross-tenant references resolve to NotFound). What is owed *here*, because it needs an /authorize endpoint to test through:

  * A request_uri issued to client A, presented at /authorize in a request naming client B, must render an error page — never a redirect. AuthRequestRepository::consume returns the row's client_id; compare it and refuse on mismatch.
  * Reloading the authorization page twice before consenting succeeds; replay after consent fails. Use peek() for rendering and consume() only at the point the user decides (FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 Note 3).
  * An expired or unknown reference renders the same error page as an already-used one. Consumed::NotFound, ::AlreadyUsed and ::Expired are distinct so a log can tell them apart; the *client* must not be able to.

The stored parameters are the JSON written by asterius_server::http::par::serialise — a hand-written projection, so adding a field there is a deliberate decision about what is stored.
close_reason: Endpoint implemented and tested; the cross-client request_uri case ast-gxh.1 owed is covered.

title: Redirect URI validation: exact match, https-only, loopback exception
description:
One function used at registration, PAR and token endpoint. FAPI 2.0 permits unregistered redirect URIs via PAR; this product deliberately keeps exact matching against the registered set (defense in depth; documented in ADR).

Spec: RFC 6749 §3.1.2.2–3.1.2.3 (registered redirect URI; comparison); RFC 9700 §4.1 (exact string matching, no pattern matching); RFC 8252 §7.3 (loopback interface redirection, any port); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.2 item 8 ('shall not allow redirect URIs that use the http scheme except for native clients that use loopback interface redirection').

Depends on: E03_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Comparison is byte-exact (RFC 3986 §6.2.1 simple string comparison) against the registered list; no prefix/pattern/case-insensitive matching (tests: trailing slash, case, added query, userinfo, IDN forms all fail).
- `https` required; `http://127.0.0.1:*` and `http://[::1]:*` accepted only for `application_type=native`, port ignored in comparison per RFC 8252 §7.3; `http://localhost` rejected.
- Fragments rejected at registration; custom schemes rejected (no public clients).
- Fuzz target `redirect_uri` with structured URI generator; proptest that normalisation is never applied.
close_reason: One exact-comparison function used by registration, and by PAR (ast-gxh.1) and the token endpoint (ast-a05.2) when they land: RedirectUri::is_registered(registered, presented, application_type). Byte-exact per RFC 3986 s6.2.1; the RFC 8252 s7.3 loopback exception varies the port and nothing else. ADR-0005 records the decision to keep exact matching even though RFC 9126 s2.4 and RFC 9700 s4.1.3 permit relaxing it for PAR-pushed URIs. Implemented by a subagent, which mutation-tested its own work (three deliberate breakages, each caught, one found by the fuzzer in 45s). I then ran an independent 25-case adversarial probe of my own choosing - prefix/suffix, /a/../cb traversal, IDN homoglyph host, 127.0.0.1:51004@evil.example, :443 vs default, a web client attempting the loopback branch, empty registered set - all behaved correctly. Deliberate behaviour change: registration now dedupes with the real comparison, so two loopback entries differing only in port are one registration; otherwise MAX_REDIRECT_URIS could hold 32 port variants of one callback and the reviewed set would not be the effective set. 347 tests.

title: Client authentication: private_key_jwt
description:
Shared authenticator used by token, PAR, introspection, revocation, device-authorization and backchannel-authentication endpoints. Keys resolved via E02_05.

Spec: OIDC Core §9 (private_key_jwt: iss=sub=client_id, aud, jti, exp; MAY contain iat); RFC 7523 §3 (JWT format and processing; jti MAY be used to reject replay); RFC 7521 §4.2 (client_assertion_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 6 (authenticate with mTLS or private_key_jwt), item 8 ('shall only accept its issuer identifier value … as a string in the aud claim'); CIBA §7.1 (backchannel endpoint MUST also accept token endpoint URL / backchannel endpoint URL as aud).

Depends on: E03_01, E02_04, E02_05

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Assertion with `aud` = issuer identifier (string) accepted; `aud` as array or token-endpoint URL rejected with `invalid_client` — except at the backchannel authentication endpoint where the three CIBA §7.1 values are accepted (documented interop note).
- `iss` ≠ `sub` ≠ authenticated `client_id` → `invalid_client`; missing `jti` → reject; `exp` more than 10 min in the future (tenant-configurable) → reject; `iat`/`nbf` skew per E02_04.
- `jti` replay within its validity window → `invalid_client` (PostgreSQL-backed replay store keyed by client_id+jti, expiring at `exp`).
- `client_id` form parameter, if present, must equal assertion `sub`; multiple client authentication methods in one request → `invalid_request` (RFC 6749 §2.3).
- Failure paths take the same time whether client exists or not (dummy verification); errors return 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` only for header-based schemes.

notes: From ast-83p.10: the acceptance 'a client of tenant A cannot authenticate at tenant B's endpoints (invalid_client)' is owed here — tenancy resolves and partitions, but there is no client model or client authentication yet to return invalid_client. Add a test that registers the same client_id in two tenants and asserts a private_key_jwt assertion minted for tenant A is rejected with invalid_client at tenant B.
close_reason: Merged to main, full gate green. Citations verified against the published texts: RFC 9700 §4.16 is Clickjacking (the ticket's FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.3 is browser-endpoint TLS/CORS and does not cover CSP); RFC 9700 §4.2.4 carries the third-party-resources rule; FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 items 6, 8 and 13 confirmed for client auth.

title: Client model & metadata validation (confidential clients only)
description:
`Client` aggregate + validating parser used by DCR, admin API and seed scripts. Defaults are the FAPI values; anything weaker is rejected, not defaulted.

Spec: RFC 7591 §2 (client metadata), §2.1 (grant_types ↔ response_types consistency); OIDC Registration §2 (application_type, subject_type, sector_identifier_uri, id_token_signed_response_alg, token_endpoint_auth_method …); RFC 9126 §6 (`require_pushed_authorization_requests`); RFC 9449 §12 (`dpop_bound_access_tokens`); RFC 9396 §9.2 (`authorization_details_types`); CIBA §4 (backchannel_* client metadata); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.2.2.1.1 (`use_mtls_endpoint_aliases`), §5.3.2.1 item 3 ('shall only support confidential clients').

Depends on: E01_03, E01_10

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- `token_endpoint_auth_method` accepted values: `private_key_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, `self_signed_tls_client_auth` (last two only with `mtls` flag); `client_secret_*` and `none` → `invalid_client_metadata`.
- `response_types` must be `["code"]`; `grant_types` ⊆ {authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, urn:openid:params:grant-type:ciba}; RFC 7591 §2.1 consistency enforced.
- `redirect_uris` required when `authorization_code` is present; each validated by E03_07 rules; `application_type=native` unlocks loopback only.
- `id_token_signed_response_alg`/`request_object_signing_alg`/`backchannel_authentication_request_signing_alg` must be in the tenant alg allow-list; `none` rejected.
- `jwks` xor `jwks_uri` required for private_key_jwt clients; `sector_identifier_uri` validated when `subject_type=pairwise` (https; JSON array that MUST include all registered redirect_uris — OIDC Registration §5 — and, for CIBA clients, the jwks_uri / notification endpoint per CIBA §4).
- `dpop_bound_access_tokens` defaults to true and cannot be set false unless `tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens` is true.
- proptest strategies for valid/invalid metadata; fuzz target `client_metadata_json`.
close_reason: Client aggregate + validating parser. Defaults are the FAPI values and anything weaker is rejected, never defaulted. Implemented by a subagent in a worktree; I merged it and then closed the schema gap it reported. Notable decisions: response_types is ['code'] or empty and nothing else, so a client_credentials client stays expressible (RFC 7591 s2.1); a non-canonical redirect URI is refused rather than rewritten, because url parses https:///cb into https://cb/ and storing raw bytes for byte-exact matching while a browser resolves something else is a real divergence; errors never echo the document, enforced by a property test; the repository re-validates on read so a row weakened by hand fails to load. I added the nine missing columns to the baseline migration (application_type, subject_type, sector_identifier_uri, the two optional signing algs, the token-binding pair, authorization_details_types, use_mtls_endpoint_aliases) plus two CHECK constraints - a client bound to neither DPoP nor a certificate cannot exist, and a sector_identifier_uri without a pairwise subject cannot exist - so upsert no longer has to refuse valid clients. 305 tests, all gates green.

title: CSPRNG token generation & secret-handling utilities (constant-time compare, zeroize)
description:
`OpaqueToken::generate(bits)` (default 256) base64url without padding; `Secret<T>` with `zeroize`; `ct_eq` wrapper (subtle) used for every secret comparison; hashing helper `sha256_hex` for at-rest storage.

Spec: FAPI 2.0 SP §5.4.1 item 4 (credentials not handled by end users ≥128 bits of entropy); RFC 6749 §10.10 (credential guessing); RFC 8628 §6.1 (user-code entropy — used later).

Depends on: E01_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Statistical sanity test on generator output (no repeats in 10^6 draws, byte distribution).
- A custom lint/grep test fails the build if `==` is used on `Secret`/`OpaqueToken` types.
- All comparisons of codes, tokens, PKCE verifiers, CSRF tokens go through `ct_eq` (reviewed checklist in PR template).
close_reason: OpaqueToken::generate defaults to 256 bits, base64url unpadded; generate_bits::<BITS>() makes the 128-bit FAPI 2.0 SP s5.4.1 floor a compile error via a const assert rather than a Result. Secret<T> and OpaqueToken deliberately do not implement PartialEq, so == on them does not compile; secret_audit.rs asks the compiler whether the trait is still absent (inherent-vs-trait associated const) so a future #[derive(PartialEq)] fails the build, and greps for the one remaining exit, secret.expose() == candidate, folding continuation lines so rustfmt cannot split a comparison into two innocent halves. I verified BOTH mechanisms myself by injecting violations: the derive produces two independent errors, and the grep half located the injected expose() comparison by file and line. ct_eq via subtle for every secret comparison; sha256_hex for at-rest lookup. Statistical test is a collision check plus Pearson chi-square over the 64-symbol alphabet, counting only the 42 fully-determined 6-bit groups (the 43rd character carries 4 bits and would make a correct generator look skewed), ~1ms. No fuzz target: from_presented validates nothing by design, so no attacker-controlled bytes become a typed value. Implemented by a subagent in a worktree; merged with conflicts in Cargo.toml, domain lib.rs and the threat model resolved by hand.

title: Client key resolution & caching (`jwks` / `jwks_uri`, SSRF guard)
description:
Resolver used by private_key_jwt, DPoP (no — DPoP uses embedded jwk), request objects, CIBA signed requests. Fetches `jwks_uri` over TLS with strict limits and caches per client.

Spec: RFC 7591 §2 (`jwks_uri` and `jwks` MUST NOT both be present); OIDC Registration §2; OIDC Core §10.1.1 (fetch JWKS again on unknown kid); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.4.2 (JWKS over TLS; recommend jwks_uri or jwks + RFC 7591/7592).

Depends on: E02_04

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Registration with both `jwks` and `jwks_uri` → `invalid_client_metadata`; `jwks_uri` must be `https` and not resolve to loopback/link-local/private ranges unless tenant allowlists it (SSRF test with DNS stub).
- Fetch: timeout 5 s, max 64 KiB, follows no redirects, requires `application/json`/`application/jwk-set+json`.
- Unknown `kid` triggers at most one refetch per 60 s per client (negative cache); hit/miss metrics.

close_reason: Client key resolution shipped: JwksFetcher port in domain, JWK-Set parsing and cache in jose, vetted HTTP adapter in server::outbound. SSRF guard verified independently against 41 adversarial URLs and addresses. Policy recorded as ADR-0006. Negative-cache gap split out as ast-mxc.8.

title: Key lifecycle & automated rotation (encrypted at rest, KMS port)
description:
States `pending → active → retiring → retired`. Per-tenant rotation schedule; private keys encrypted with a KEK obtained from a `Kek` port (local file / env for dev, cloud KMS adapters later). Separate keys per purpose (id_token/access_token signing, SET signing may share; encryption keys separate).

Spec: OIDC Core §10.1.1 (rotation of asymmetric signing keys: publish new key, then sign with it; keep old for verification); FAPI 2.0 SP §6.8 (key compromise: automated regular rotation, single-purpose keys).

Depends on: E02_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rotation test: tokens signed before rotation still verify via JWKS until grace end; new tokens use the new `kid`; retired keys are not published.
- Private key material at rest is ciphertext (test reads DB row and asserts it does not parse as JWK).
- Admin API endpoint triggers rotation; audit event emitted; concurrent rotations serialised with a DB lock.
- Same key is never used for both signing and encryption (enforced by `purpose` column + test).
notes: From ast-mxc.2: the JWKS endpoint currently uses a fixed Cache-Control max-age of 300s (crates/server/src/http/protocol.rs, JWKS_MAX_AGE). The acceptance for mxc.2 wants max-age = rotation-interval/4, which needs the rotation schedule this ticket owns. Wire it when the schedule exists, and make sure the cache lifetime stays shorter than the retiring grace period - a verifier must refetch before the key it holds stops being published.
close_reason: States pending/active/retiring/retired with a per-tenant schedule; private keys sealed with AES-GCM under a KEK from a Kek port (LocalKek for dev, async so a cloud KMS fits). Implemented by a subagent in a worktree. Verified independently: I read the stored bytes out of PostgreSQL and they are opaque (73d66d26..., not a DER SEQUENCE), nonce is 96 bits, length is PKCS#8 + 16-byte GCM tag, kek_id is derived, and a rotation leaves active+pending which is publish-before-sign. Notable: RandomizedNonceKey means the code physically cannot supply a nonce twice, backed by a unique index on (kek_id, nonce); AAD binds tenant/kid/purpose/alg length-prefixed so a moved or relabelled row is undecryptable; schedule periods are bigint seconds not interval, because a month has no fixed length and a grace period must not differ in February. The agent's first concurrency test passed without the lock, so it demoted it to an idempotence test and wrote one that actually fails when the lock is removed. Spec correction accepted and verified against the Final text: key compromise is FAPI 2.0 SP s6.8, not s6.7 (s6.7 is Client Impersonating Resource Owner) - I corrected 2 citations in crates/domain/src/audit and 5 in docs/BACKLOG.md. 381 tests. Runtime wiring is a separate ticket (filed): the binary still uses LocalKeyStore.

title: JWT verification service (typ, crit, skew window, duplicate-kid selection)
description:
One verifier used for client assertions, DPoP proofs, request objects, id_token_hint, CIBA signed requests, logout tokens received in tests. Callers pass an expected `typ`, allowed algs, expected `iss`/`aud`, and a key resolver.

Spec: RFC 8725 §3.1–3.3 (alg verification, key/alg binding), §3.5 (crit), §3.8–3.9 (validate all claims, use UTC), §3.11 (explicit typ); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.3.2.1 item 13 ('shall accept JWTs with an iat or nbf timestamp between 0 and 10 seconds in the future but shall reject JWTs with an iat or nbf timestamp greater than 60 seconds in the future'); §5.4.3 (duplicate kid selection algorithm).

Depends on: E02_01

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Missing or mismatching `typ` rejected when the context requires one (`dpop+jwt`, `oauth-authz-req+jwt`, `at+jwt`, `logout+jwt`, `secevent+jwt`).
- Unknown `crit` parameter → reject; `alg` outside caller's allow-list → reject; key type/alg mismatch → reject (RS/HS confusion test).
- Clock skew: iat/nbf up to +10 s accepted; +11..+60 s accepted only if tenant config raises the window (max 60); +61 s rejected; expired `exp` rejected with 0 s leeway by default.
- Duplicate-kid test set: verifier iterates candidate keys matching `kid` and selects by `alg`/`kty`/`crv`/`use` per FAPI 2.0 SP §5.4.3.
- Maximum JWT size 8 KiB (configurable); fuzz target on claims parsing.
close_reason: One verifier for every JWT the server accepts (client assertions, DPoP proofs, request objects, id_token_hint, CIBA, logout tokens). Policy has no Default - typ and the algorithm list are decisions a caller must make. Checks ordered so cost precedes trust: size before parsing, structure and crit, algorithm against the caller's list, signature against a resolver-chosen key, claims last. FAPI 2.0 SP s5.3.2.1 item 13 implemented exactly: iat/nbf 0-10s ahead accepted, >60s refused, and with_future_skew clamps rather than rejects so a misconfiguration yields a compliant server. exp has zero leeway; a string NumericDate is not a NumericDate. aud checked in both RFC 7519 s4.1.3 spellings. s5.4.3 duplicate-kid handling: candidates filtered by algorithm then each tried, with a test that puts the decoy first so passing cannot be an ordering accident. 8 KiB default size cap, configurable. jws::Header.kid became Optional because a DPoP proof carries jwk instead (RFC 9449 s4.2). 48 jose tests; jwt_verify fuzz target added, coverage gate at 8 parsers.

title: KeyStore/Signer port + josekit adapter with algorithm allow-list
description:
Trait `Signer { fn sign(&self, header: Header, claims: &[u8]) -> Result<Jws> }` and `KeyStore` (active key per (tenant, purpose, alg), lookup by kid). josekit adapter with aws-lc-rs/ring backends. Every issued JWT sets `kid`, `alg` and an explicit `typ`.

Spec: FAPI 2.0 SP §5.4.1 items 1–3 (RFC 8725 adherence; PS256/ES256/EdDSA(Ed25519) only; no `none`; RSA ≥2048; EC ≥224 bits); RFC 8725 §3.1 (verify alg), §3.2 (restrict algs), §3.11 (explicit typ); RFC 7515/7517/7518.

Depends on: E01_01, E01_03

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Constructing a signer with `none`, `HS*`, or (without `compat.rs256`) `RS256` is a compile-time or startup error; unit tests cover each.
- Ed25519 keys sign/verify (EdDSA), P-256 (ES256), RSA-2048/3072/4096 (PS256); RSA-1024 key import rejected.
- Property test: sign→verify round-trip for random payloads and all enabled algs; tampering any byte fails verification.
- Fuzz target `jwt_compact` (header/payload/signature splitting, base64url) runs clean 10 min.
close_reason: JOSE on aws-lc-rs (ADR-0004: josekit pulls OpenSSL, which deny.toml bans). SigningAlgorithm is a closed 3-variant enum in asterius-domain so asterius-oidc can publish it in metadata without depending on an adapter; none/HS256/RS256 are not representable. SigningKey generates/imports/exports PKCS#8 for EdDSA, ES256, PS256 with the FAPI 2.0 SP s5.4.1 RSA-2048 floor checked on both paths; public_jwk emits RFC 7517/7518 members and no private ones. JWS compact serialisation per RFC 7515 s7.1: verification uses the key's algorithm and requires the header to agree (RFC 8725 s3.1-3.2), signing covers the encoded bytes so a re-encoded header cannot reuse a signature, explicit typ required (s3.11), any crit refused. LocalKeyStore implements the KeyStore and Signer ports with RFC 7638 thumbprint kids - verified against the RFC's published test vector - and rotation that retires rather than replaces so pre-rotation tokens still verify. 28 jose tests including per-byte signature tampering across all three algorithms. jws_parse fuzz target registered; coverage gate at 7 parsers.

title: JWKS endpoint (`jwks_uri`)
description:

Spec: OIDC Discovery §3 (`jwks_uri`: keys used to sign ID Tokens; `use` parameter); OIDC Core §10.1.1 (key rotation via JWKS); FAPI 2.0 SP §5.4.2 (serve only over TLS; should not use `x5u`/`jku`; should not serve multiple keys with the same `kid`).

Definition of done (project rule): spec-derived or conformance-suite test passes; fuzz target exists for every new parser/validator; threat-model note updated; no new `unsafe`; generated crypto/parsing code is not done until a human has read the cited spec sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- Response never contains `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi` or symmetric `k` (schema test).
- Test rejects a key set with duplicate `kid` at generation time; retiring keys remain published for the configured grace period after rotation.
- `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<rotation/4>`; ETag supported.
- Emitted JWS headers never include `x5u`/`jku` (unit test on header builder).
notes: Implemented and merged in d97a57d; 332 tests green. Held open only by the ast-mxc.3 dependency: the JWKS Cache-Control max-age should derive from the rotation interval (currently a fixed 300s) and the retiring grace period comes from the same schedule. Close once ast-mxc.3 lands and that is wired.
